activity_context.topic_title: Row Operations on 2x2 Matrices as Products of Elementary Matrices

feedback.problem: Let  $E=[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}].$ Find the row operation that, when applied to a $2\times 2$ matrix $A,$ gives the result of the product $EA.$
feedback.worked_solution:
The matrix $E$ is obtained by multiplying the first row of the identity matrix  by $3$:

$$
\begin{aligned}I & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] & {R}_{1} & :=3{R}_{1} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}3 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}] \\  & =E\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $EA$ is equivalent to applying the row operation ${R}_{1}:=3{R}_{1}$ to $A.$
